title: TSMC Reports Oct. 15. It's the Best Early Read on Nvidia's Next Quarter.
source_used: The Motley Fool via Yahoo Finance (full text from the pre-fetched file)
key_facts: TSMC reports its third-quarter results on Thursday 15 Oct 2026; the quarter ran July to September.
TSMC guided for third-quarter revenue of $44.6 billion to $45.8 billion, about 12% above the second quarter and 37% above a year earlier at the midpoint.
TSMC's July revenue rose around 45% and August revenue about 53% year over year in New Taiwan dollars.
Nvidia has guided for about $108 billion in fiscal third-quarter revenue, plus or minus 2%, roughly 89% growth against the $57.0 billion of a year earlier, slower than 106% in the previous quarter.
High-performance computing made up 66% of TSMC's second-quarter revenue; TSMC's chief executive C.C. Wei said in July that packaging capacity is so tight it limits customers' growth.
TSMC's AI figures include competitors' custom chips and cannot show what Nvidia charges; 'Customer A', reportedly Nvidia, was 19% of TSMC's 2025 revenue.
TSMC raised its 2026 revenue growth forecast from close to 30% in January to above 30% in April and just above 40% in July.
quote_evidence: I think it's the best early look investors will have at Nvidia's next quarter.
But it covers the whole AI chip market, not just Nvidia, and that limits what it can show.
"[O]ur packaging capacity is so tight that now it limits my customers' growth," TSMC Chairman and CEO C.C. Wei said in July, on TSMC's second-quarter earnings call.
why_it_matters_hint: TSMC's report will give an early read on AI chip demand, though it cannot show Nvidia's pricing or isolate Nvidia's share.
event_date: Preview dated 11 Oct 2026; TSMC reports 15 Oct 2026
notes: Opinion-style preview by Daniel Sparks of The Motley Fool, carried on Yahoo Finance; the stock-valuation and stock-pick passages are left out of the entry (no buy or sell advice). TSMC's September revenue (up more than 50 percent, reported separately) is not in this text.
